function: Multi-agent DRL allocates sub-channels, bandwidth and transmit power for UE-HAP uplink and HAP-LEO-sat association, power, sub-carriers; LSTM predicts future channel environment state (p. 10, 11, 12).
system: NTN uplinks: 300 single-antenna UEs, 3 HAPs, 12 LEO satellites (800-1200 km); OFDM UE-HAP, NOMA HAP-LEO-sat; 30 GHz centre frequency; no RIS (p. 4, 14).
method: Multi-agent deep Q-learning with LSTM environment predictor (DeepRMARL) for UE-HAP; double DQN with prioritized experience replay (MADDQN-PP) for HAP-LEO-sat; reinforcement learning by environment interaction (p. 9, 11, 12).
data_channel: Simulated: free-space path loss with fading factor Rcf at 30 GHz; LEO/NTN parameters from 3GPP TR 38.811; LSTM trained on simulated observations; no measured data (p. 6, 14).
test_conditions: Agents trained 200 episodes; LSTM tested on values unseen in training; sweeps over UE count, sub-channels, bandwidth, power, fading, LEO count; retraining not stated (p. 14, 16).
baselines: UE-HAP: Q-learning RL channel allocation [24], E-DNN scheduling [25], alternating optimization AOT [16]; HAP-LEO-sat: standard DQN, matching game MGA [13], random matching, random policy (p. 14, 15).
metrics: Uplink sum rate, transmission latency, Jain fairness index, system utility, link load, LSTM prediction RMSE/MSE and accuracy (about 92.8%), execution time (p. 14, 16, 18).
complexity: Complexity order given for both uplinks, including O(|L| log|L| Iepisode NNN) for MADDQN-PP (p. 14); execution time versus UEs and LEO-sat in Fig. 20 (p. 18).
q1_support: p. 6: "defines the channel fading parameter to represent how much the channel is affected" (own model: free-space path loss and a scalar fading factor); p. 14: "Other parameters used for LEO-sat and NTN in general can be found at [36]" (TR 38.811 gives parameters only, not the channel model).
q2_support: p. 16: "the values that the validated model has never seen before" is a held-out part of the same simulation; no test in another scenario without retraining is stated, and the UE-count and bandwidth sweeps (p. 16, 17) do not say whether agents were retrained.
q3_support: p. 14: "Benchmark-1 is proposed in [24], in which wireless channels are intelligently assigned by Q-Learning-based RL"; p. 15: "Benchmark-3 is proposed in [16], utilizing an alternating optimization technique (AOT) as a conventional optimization method"; p. 16: "AOT scheme in [16] has a similar trend but with lower average throughput values".
q4_support: p. 14: "the computational complexity of resource allocation scheme for both uplinks is" followed by the order expression; p. 18: "Fig. 20(a) illustrates the required execution time for the DeepRMARL+LSTM compared with the benchmarks".
q5_support: p. 14: "300 UEs are randomly distributed in 3 sub-areas": the data are self-simulated; the only external reference for parameters is the 3GPP document [36] (p. 14); no code or data link or DOI appears in the paper.
notes: The PDF is the paper of the DOI (p. 1: Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/TWC.2025.3565774). Passes above_phy because the agents learn transmit power, bandwidth and sub-carrier allocation in aerial and satellite links jointly with association (p. 10, 12); passes system because NTN admits single-antenna links (p. 4). Area 6 wins over 2 (LSTM channel prediction). q1 is borderline: TR 38.811 is cited for LEO/NTN parameters and the Doppler formula (p. 7, 14, Table II) but not as the channel model, so it is marked 0; reviewer to confirm. Table II read from the page image (p. 14).
